Done. Summary of the task and fix:

## Cause
`CommandParser` (django/core/management/base.py) carries two extra settings — `missing_args_message` and `called_from_command_line` — that make argument errors raise a friendly `CommandError`/usage message instead of a raw traceback. But `add_subparsers()` (inherited from `argparse`) builds subparsers with the plain `ArgumentParser` class (`type(parser)` is only set by argparse's default `_parser_class`), so subparsers lost both settings. Any error inside a subparser (e.g. a missing required positional in `cheeses create`) fell through to `CommandParser.error` → `raise CommandError` with no CLI handling → stack trace.

## Fix (minimal, source only — `django/core/management/base.py`)
1. Added `from functools import partial` to the imports.
2. Overrode `add_subparsers()` on `CommandParser` so the returned subparser action:
   - sets `required` from kwargs (argparse only honors `required` at call time otherwise),
   - sets `_parser_class` to a `partial(CommandParser, missing_args_message=..., called_from_command_line=...)`, so every subparser created via `add_parser()` inherits the error-formatting behavior.

No tests were modified or added; nothing committed; changes are in the working tree.
